Article Text:
Fadnavis said people deserved clarity on what had happened.

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis on Monday urged Union home minister Amit Shah to expedite the investigation into the plane crash that killed former deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar and make the findings public at the earliest.Speaking at a programme in Pune where Shah unveiled a bust of the late NCP leader at the Pune Zilla Parishad (ZP) office, Fadnavis said, "Eight to 10 months have passed, and a major investigation is underway. Teams from different countries and international agencies are also assisting in the probe. However, the confusion and apprehensions in the minds of ordinary people in Maharashtra must be addressed. The investigation report should come out at the earliest. "Raising questions about the circumstances of the crash, the chief minister said people deserved clarity on what had happened and called for strict action if anyone was found guilty."People want to know what exactly happened. Was it an accident or was there something else behind it? If anyone is found guilty, they must be given the strictest punishment. And if it was an accident, the anguish and questions in the minds of ordinary people must at least be addressed."Ajit Pawar died on January 28 this year when a Learjet 45 aircraft operated by VSR Ventures crashed while attempting to land at Baramati airport. The aircraft was flying from Mumbai to Baramati. Four others were also killed in the crash.The Maharashtra CID and the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), under the Union civil aviation ministry, are conducting separate investigations into the incident.Following Ajit Pawar's death, his wife Sunetra Pawar took over as the NCP president and became Maharashtra's deputy chief minister.
Article Summary: Devendra Fadnavis said people deserved clarity on what had happened. Ajit Pawar died on January 28 this year when a Learjet 45 aircraft operated by VSR Ventures crashed while attempting to land at Baramati airport. Four others were also killed in the crash.

Article Title: Union minister Suresh Gopi says diesel, price cuts 'not possible right away'; cites Rs 42,000 crore losses
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union Minister Suresh Gopi has said petrol and diesel prices cannot be reduced immediately, citing Rs 42,000 crore in losses suffered by oil companies and disruptions in fuel supply.Gopi said oil companies had suffered losses of Rs 42,000 crore, making an immediate reduction difficult. Any relief through lower retail prices would have to take these accumulated losses into account, he said.“We may wish for prices to come down the next day. But technically it is not possible right away,” the minister told reporters at Meenambakkam airport, as quoted by ANI. “Oil companies have already incurred losses of Rs 42,000 crore. All this needs to be compensated.”He suggested that state governments could offer some relief by lowering taxes on petrol. Referring to recent price increases, Gopi said fuel had also become costlier in Kerala and Karnataka, while he was unable to explain the increase in Tamil Nadu.The minister also flagged problems in the availability of petroleum products, saying the government was working to address them. “There is chaos in the supply of petroleum products.We are doing whatever needs to be done to fix it,” he said.The supply concerns come against the backdrop of the Middle East conflict and its impact on energy markets. Separately, Karnataka industries minister MB Patil has accused the Centre of worsening the ethanol sector's crisis by setting higher blending targets without ensuring adequate procurement. He alleged that the government was now refusing to buy even 20-30 per cent of the ethanol produced and called for an investigation into alleged irregularities in the blending programme.
Article Summary: Gopi said oil companies had suffered losses of Rs 42,000 crore, making an immediate reduction difficult. Any relief through lower retail prices would have to take these accumulated losses into account. Karnataka industries minister MB Patil has accused the Centre of worsening the ethanol sector's crisis.

Article Title: Parents fled Mozambique with unregistered newborn; 26 yrs later, Gujarat woman gets Indian passport
Article Text:
Dolly Vadalia, brought to India from Mozambique as a newborn, received her passport after a 26-year citizenship battle

NEW DELHI: A 26-year-old woman from Gujarat, whose Indian parents brought her to the country as an unregistered newborn while fleeing floods in Mozambique, has finally received an Indian passport after a prolonged citizenship battle. Dolly Vadalia received the passport on November 11, following a Union home ministry memorandum recognising her as an Indian citizen, news agency PTI reported citing her brother-in-law Ronak Vadalia on Monday.Born on February 18, 2000, in Xai-Xai, Mozambique, Dolly was just 18 to 20 days old when her parents evacuated her from the country after a tropical cyclone triggered massive floods. The family returned to India and settled in Rajkot, their hometown.Dolly's citizenship status became a hurdle after she married Khilankumar Vadalia, a Rajkot resident employed in Canada, in 2023. Her inability to obtain an Indian passport kept the couple separated.Her three passport applications, filed in 2023 and 2025, were rejected because she could not establish her Indian citizenship through the required documents. Authorities sought proof of cancellation of her emergency certificate or consular registration of her birth.The matter was subsequently taken up with Lok Sabha MPs Ramesh Dhaduk and Parshottam Rupala, who forwarded it to the Rajkot collectorate, the Gandhinagar secretariat, the MHA and the MEA, Ronak said as cited by PTI.The MEA sought the MHA's opinion. In October last year, the home ministry reiterated that under Section 4(1)(b) of the Citizenship Act, 1955, a child born outside India must have their birth registered at an Indian consulate within one year to claim citizenship by descent. Although Dolly had an Aadhaar card, it was not sufficient to establish her eligibility for an Indian passport, Ronak said.On April 30 this year, a single-judge bench of the Gujarat high court observed that Dolly's parents had not followed the mandatory birth registration procedure. It held that she was neither an Indian citizen by birth nor by descent under Sections 3 and 4 of the Act."The court advised us to apply for citizenship; however, we could not file an application initially because we lacked a valid passport — a mandatory requirement for the process," Ronak said, explaining why the family subsequently approached a division bench.Following a background check and verification, the Indian embassy in Mozambique and the MHA issued a memorandum."Based on this, Dolly's birth was registered with the Indian High Commission in Maputo, Mozambique, in November. Using that certificate, we applied for a passport, which we finally received last week," he said.
Article Summary: Dolly Vadalia received the passport on November 11, following a Union home ministry memorandum recognising her as an Indian citizen. Born on February 18, 2000, in Xai-Xai, Mozambique, her parents evacuated her from the country after a tropical cyclone triggered massive floods. Her inability to obtain an Indian passport kept the couple separated.

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Monday described the death of former Maharashtra deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar as an “irreparable loss” to the state. He further praised his work ethic and understanding of governance would serve as a “university” for future generations of political leaders.Shah made the remarks after unveiling a bust of Pawar at the Zilla Parishad office premises in Pune, in the presence of Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.“The sudden and untimely passing away of 'Dada' is an irreparable loss, not only for Maharashtra, but specifically for the regions of Pune, Baramati, Pimpri and Chinchwad,” Shah said.He added that the void left by Pawar's death could not be filled even with collective efforts over several decades. The bust, he said, would inspire future generations to learn from the late leader's work and contributions.Recalling his association with Pawar, Shah described him as a close friend and colleague who had a deep understanding of development, Panchayati Raj, cooperatives, agriculture and urban development.“I found Ajit Pawar very clear and straightforward in all political negotiations,” Shah said.He also praised Pawar's role during the Covid-19 pandemic, taking a swipe at the administration led by then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.Shah said there was no communication with Thackeray during the crisis, but Pawar remained accessible over the landline at the state secretariat and ensured that the government's relief work continued, as quoted by PTI.Describing Pawar as an “encyclopaedia” of the cooperative sector, Shah said his knowledge extended to sugar factories, milk unions, primary agricultural credit societies and cooperative banks, as well as their administrative challenges.Shah also credited Pawar's entry into the BJP-led Mahayuti alliance with helping stabilise the ruling coalition in Maharashtra. Pawar, along with several NCP leaders, had joined the alliance in July 2023, triggering a vertical split in the party then headed by Sharad Pawar.The Union minister said Pawar had made a significant contribution to the transformation of Baramati, his constituency and the Pawar family's political stronghold in Pune district.Meanwhile, CM Fadnavis requested Shah to expedite the investigation into the plane crash that killed Pawar and sought the release of the final report. The Maharashtra CID and the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), under the civil aviation ministry, are conducting separate inquiries into the crash.Ajit Pawar died on January 28 this year when the aircraft carrying him crashed while attempting to land at Baramati airport in Pune district.

Article Title: Faster shift to electricity can save India Rs 9.6 lakh crore in fuel imports annually by FY35: Study
Article Text:
The shift could translate into annual savings of Rs 9.6 lakh crore by FY2035

Power infrastructure is the big challenge

MUMBAI: India's dependence on imported oil, gas and coal could be substantially reduced by accelerating electrification, potentially bringing down the annual fossil fuel import bill by more than 40% to Rs 7.4 lakh crore by FY2035, against Rs 17 lakh crore projected under the current trajectory, according to a new study released on Monday.The shift could translate into annual savings of Rs 9.6 lakh crore by FY2035, while reducing India's exposure to international oil-price shocks, geopolitical disruptions and currency volatility. The study projects that direct fossil fuel imports could be brought down to zero by FY2045, against an estimated annual import expenditure of Rs 23.3 lakh crore under a business-as-usual scenario.The report, Decoupling from Fossil Fuel Imports: An Accelerated Electrification Scenario for India,by research firm Climate Compatible Futures, argues that electrification must move beyond renewable power generation to transforming how energy is consumed in transport, industry, agriculture and buildings.The urgency is underlined by India's recent experience with global energy disruptions. Shipping constraints through the Strait of Hormuz since February 2026 pushed Brent crude prices above $100 a barrel. India's crude import bill rose 48% year-on-year during April-August, while the rupee depreciated nearly 8% during 2026 to a record low of 96.90 against the dollar.India spent $174.9 billion on crude oil and petroleum products in FY2026, accounting for about 22% of its total import bill."Every few years, an oil shock somewhere else becomes a rupee crisis at home. We have treated this as a problem to be managed, through reserves and rate decisions. Electrification lets India solve it at the root," said Dr Manish Ram, director, Climate Compatible Futures.The study identifies transport as the single biggest opportunity to reduce India's crude oil dependence. It estimates that 45% of the sector's fuel demand could shift away from fossil fuels by FY2035 through electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, buses, cars, urban fleets and delivery vehicles.By FY2045, the shift could reach 93%, with electricity, green hydrogen and bioenergy replacing much of the petroleum currently used. Sustainable aviation fuel and alternative fuels would be important for segments that are difficult to electrify directly.The residential and commercial sector could shift 44% of its fuel demand away from fossil fuels by FY2035. The proposed pathway envisages phasing out LPG and natural gas in homes and commercial establishments by FY2045 through electric cooking, appliances and efficient cooling systems.Agriculture and other uses could achieve a 47% shift by FY2035 through electric irrigation pumps, farm machinery and dependable rural electricity supply.Industry, meanwhile, could shift 28% of its fuel demand by FY2035 and 61% by FY2045. Electric boilers, heat pumps and furnaces, along with green hydrogen for steel and chemical manufacturing, are among the proposed solutions. The study recommends concessional finance and cluster-based technical support to help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) bear the cost of switching technologies.The transition would require a substantial expansion of clean electricity generation, transmission, distribution and storage. The study estimates that total energy demand under the accelerated pathway would reach 15,785 billion units (BU) by FY2045, compared with 13,059 BU under the business-as-usual scenario. This higher requirement partly reflects the additional 2,726 BU of electricity needed to produce green hydrogen.Electricity's share of total energy demand could rise from 29% currently to 54% by FY2035 and 76% by FY2045. Direct electricity, green hydrogen and bioenergy together could displace about 87% of the fossil fuel demand projected under the business-as-usual scenario by FY2045.The study calls for a national, sector-specific electrification roadmap with FY2035 and FY2045 milestones, accelerated adoption of electric vehicles, dedicated industrial electrification programmes and advance planning of renewable generation, transmission and storage.India already has a foundation for this transition: 99.6% of its broad-gauge railway network has been electrified, electric vehicles accounted for 13.11% of vehicle sales in September 2026, and non-fossil sources account for more than half of installed power capacity."India does not need to be persuaded to electrify. It is already doing it. The real question is whether it electrifies fast enough to change its import reliance," Ram said.The report, however, clarifies that zero direct fossil fuel imports would not mean an end to fossil fuel consumption. Industrial coal and some aviation and shipping fuels, together accounting for less than 8% of projected energy demand, would continue to be used but would be met through domestic production.The projections are scenario-based, not guaranteed outcomes. Import expenditure estimates use FY2025 fuel prices, and achieving the targets would depend on technology adoption, affordable finance, reliable electricity supply and the availability of sustainable bioenergy feedstock.
Article Summary: India's dependence on imported oil, gas and coal could be substantially reduced by accelerating electrification. The shift could translate into annual savings of Rs 9.6 lakh crore by FY2035. The study identifies transport as the single biggest opportunity to reduce India's crude oil dependence.

Article Title: ‘Does Bengal belong to Bengalis or rogue Biharis?’ TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee's remarks on Chhath spark row
Article Text:
Chhath Puja arrangements trigger TMC-BJP row in West Bengal

BJP minister hits back at TMC

Suvendu Adhikari defends Chhath arrangements

Chhath celebrations across the country

NEW DELHI: A political row has erupted in West Bengal after Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Kalyan Banerjee criticised the BJP government over arrangements for Chhath Puja , alleging that the state had been “taken over” by non-Bengalis and accusing the ruling party of undermining Bengali culture.Speaking to reporters on Saturday, Banerjee questioned the scale of decorations at Howrah railway station for the festival, alleging that similar arrangements were not made for Durga Puja.“Are there Bengalis in West Bengal anymore? Does West Bengal belong to Bengalis or rogue Biharis? Does practising Sanatan dharma mean cutting off Bengalis and establishing Biharis? BJP will destroy the Bengali culture. I was surprised to see Howrah station decked up like that for Chhath. Such decorations are not put up for Durga Puja,” he said, as quoted by news agency ANI.The TMC leader further alleged that Bengalis had become “second-category citizens” in the state and warned that they would “cease to exist” if the situation continued for another five years.His remarks drew a sharp response from West Bengal minister Indranil Khan, who accused the TMC of pursuing divisive politics and questioned its record on issues concerning Bengali culture and people.Khan alleged that neither the previous TMC government nor the Left government had adequately served the interests of Bengali people.“Is it Bengali culture to carry Maa Kali on a prison van? Is it Bengali culture to stop Durga Visarjan for Muharram? Was it in the interest of Bengalis to fire bullets on students demanding the appointment of a teacher for Bengali language at Daribhit? They do divisive politics and nothing else. Had they worked in the interest of Bengalis, 15 years of TMC rule and 34 years of Left rule would have made something good out of Bengal,” he said.Defending the arrangements for Chhath Puja, the minister said people from different communities and cultural backgrounds contributed to the country and had the right to celebrate their festivals.“Ek Bharat Shresht Bharat. People of various diversities contribute towards the country...Everyone has the right to participate in their festival, and it is the duty of the government to stand with them. But TMC and Left didn't do their duty,” Khan said.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari also defended the government's arrangements for the festival, describing Chhath as a celebration of the Sanatan tradition and rejecting attempts to associate it exclusively with any one community or state.Adhikari participated in Chhath Puja celebrations at Ramkrishnapur Ghat in Howrah on Sunday. He said at least one crore followers of the Sanatan tradition were observing the festival and that participation was not limited to Hindi speakers.“At least one crore followers of the Sanatan tradition are observing this. It is not just Hindi speakers; all followers of the Sanatan tradition are participating in Chhath—a grand festival of faith and tradition,” he told reporters.He said the government had made arrangements for Chhath along the lines of preparations for Durga Puja, Kali Puja and Diwali, adding that the facilities for the festival were well organised.Adhikari also accused critics of indulging in “vote-bank appeasement politics” and described their approach as narrow-minded.“They would claim that the Ganpati festival belongs only to the Marathis, that Chhath belongs only to the people of Bihar, or that Ram Navami belongs only to Uttar Pradesh,” he said, adding that people had rejected such divisions and made it clear that “at the end of the day, we are all Indians”.The political exchanges came as devotees across the country marked the final day of the four-day Chhath festival by offering 'arghya' to the rising Sun.Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings to devotees on Monday, saying the festival brought together steadfast resolve and spiritual practice.In a post on X, he said, “Today, the four-day ritual of the grand festival of Chhath concluded with the offering of prayers to the rising sun. This divine festival dedicated to nature witnessed a remarkable confluence of steadfast resolve and spiritual practice. I pray to Chhathi Maiya to bestow her blessings on all the devotees observing the fast, as well as on my family members across the country.”Political leaders also participated in celebrations in several states. In Bihar, BJP national president Nitin Nabin was seen carrying a 'daura' as his wife performed the rituals in Patna, while chief minister Samrat Chaudhary offered prayers at a ghat in Munger.In Chhattisgarh, Chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai and his wife participated in the rituals in Kunkuri, where a groundbreaking ceremony for a Chhath Ghat was also held. BJP MP Ravi Kishan offered morning prayers in Gorakhpur, while party MP Manoj Tiwari participated in the celebrations at Sonia Vihar Ghat in Delhi.
Article Summary: TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee accuses ruling party of undermining Bengali culture. West Bengal minister Indranil Khan accuses TMC of pursuing divisive politics. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari defends the government's arrangements for the festival.

Article Title: 'Inappropriate to lecture India on democracy': Meloni ally hits back at Italian leader's BJP vote theft jibe
Article Text:
Italian legislator Deborah Bergamini criticised Giacomo Filibeck for interfering in India's internal matters

Bergamini invokes India-Italy strategic partnership

Filibeck backs Rahul Gandhi, BJP accuses Congress of seeking foreign help

NEW DELHI: Italian legislator Deborah Bergamini has criticised Giacomo Filibeck, secretary general of the Party of European Socialists (PES), over his “Vote thieves, step down from your seats” remark targeting the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), saying foreign political representatives should not intervene in the domestic political debate of a friendly country.In a post on X, Bergamini said India had its own political institutions and judiciary to address domestic political disputes. She also pointed to the special strategic partnership between Italy and India, arguing that it was inappropriate for European representatives to lecture the country on democracy.Deborah Bergamini is a member and national deputy secretary of Forza Italia, a centre-right political party that is part of the governing coalition supporting Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.Her remarks came after Filibeck, while attending the Bharat Summit 2026 organised by the Congress in Hyderabad, accused the BJP-led government of undermining democracy and expressed support for Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and the Congress.“An Italian representative from the European Socialists and Democrats group, while attending a meeting organised by the Indian National Congress party , attacked Prime Minister Modi’s BJP, declaring: ‘Vote thieves, step down from your seats.’This stems from the Indian opposition’s criticism of the ruling majority regarding a long-overdue revision of electoral rolls—a process intended to remove duplicate entries, the names of deceased individuals, and those who have relocated,” Bergamini said.The revision of electoral rolls has been a point of contention between the opposition and the BJP-led government.“I believe that, in a democracy, everyone is free to put forward whatever arguments or accusations they see fit—provided, of course, that they can substantiate them,” she added.Bergamini said Italy and India shared a “special strategic partnership”, with cooperation across several sectors, and argued that foreign representatives should refrain from intervening in India's internal political discussions.“Furthermore, in instances like this, it is inappropriate to intervene in the domestic political debate of a major friendly nation—a country with which our own has established a ‘special strategic partnership,’ fostering deep cooperation across all sectors,” she said.She also questioned the appropriateness of European representatives commenting on India's democratic processes, citing the scale of its electorate.“Moreover, as Europeans, we find it inappropriate to lecture on democracy a nation that enables 970 million citizens to cast their votes. India possesses its own political institutions and judiciary; any conflicts or disputes should be addressed and resolved in accordance with the established rules of democracy,” Bergamini said.Filibeck had said that international gatherings were important to draw global attention to what he described as challenges facing Indian democracy.“Democracy is under attack in India, and we need to defend it, and the best way to defend it is to stand by Rahul Gandhi and the Indian Congress Party,” he told news agency ANI on the sidelines of the summit.He also said the PES, the Congress and other political movements across the world were part of a progressive alliance committed to social justice, climate justice, human rights and democracy.The remarks drew criticism from BJP leaders. BJP national spokesperson and national media co-in-charge Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress MP of seeking foreign interference in India's domestic political affairs.In a post on X, Bhandari alleged that Rahul was seeking “regime change with foreign help” and acting on behalf of foreign powers seeking instability in the country.Union minister Kiren Rijiju also took an indirect swipe at the Congress over the involvement of foreign political figures in India's domestic affairs.Reacting to the controversy in a post on X, he wrote, “Have you ever seen anyone laughing when India is insulted by a foreigner? I'm not asking about which Indian goes abroad to insult India.”Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao had also criticised Rahul’s remarks on democracy at the summit and demanded an apology.Referring to the Raebareli MP's statement that democracy had been destroyed in India since 2014, Rao cited the Emergency and the dismissal of elected state governments during Congress rule.The Bharat Summit 2026 has brought together around 1,000 delegates, policymakers and thinkers from 70 countries to discuss global geopolitics, democracy, climate change, artificial intelligence and progressive politics.
Article Summary: Deborah Bergamini is a member and national deputy secretary of Forza Italia, a centre-right political party that is part of the governing coalition supporting Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. She criticised Giacomo Filibeck, secretary general of the Party of European Socialists (PES), over his “Vote thieves, step down from your seats” remark targeting the Bharatiya Janata Party.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will travel to Manila on Monday for a two-day visit to attend the 23rd India-Asean Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit. Maritime security, regional stability and expanding trade ties are expected to be key focus areas at the meetings.Announcing his visit to Manila, PM Modi said in a post on X, "Will be in Manila, Philippines later today and tomorrow to attend the following programmes: 23rd Asean-India Summit. 21st East Asia Summit.""India attaches immense importance to close friendship with Asean nations. I’m also looking forward to interacting with the Indian community based in the Philippines," he added.The visit comes as India seeks to strengthen its strategic engagement with Southeast Asia amid rapid geopolitical changes in the Indo-Pacific. The Philippines, which is chairing the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) this year, is hosting both summits.According to the ministry of external affairs (MEA), Prime Minister will attend a dinner hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr on November 16 before participating in the India-Asean Summit and the East Asia Summit process on November 17.Bilateral meetings with other leaders are also being planned.Speaking at a special briefing, MEA secretary (East) Rudrendra Tandon said India's engagement with Asean, both as a regional grouping and with individual member countries, was an important part of its Act East policy."We strongly believe that as an Indian Ocean country that abuts this very important Southeast Asian maritime zone, a strong strategic relationship with the Asean member states, as a collective as well as individually, is good for both of us," Tandon said.Maritime cooperation is expected to feature prominently in the discussions, particularly as India and Asean share adjoining maritime zones and face common regional security challenges.India and Asean marked 2026 as the Year of Maritime Cooperation, with several activities aimed at highlighting their shared maritime interests.New Delhi believes closer strategic cooperation with Southeast Asian countries will help both sides deal with changing geopolitical developments and contribute to peace and stability across Asia.The East Asia Summit, an Asean-led forum involving regional and major global powers, will provide another platform for leaders to discuss international security issues and matters of common concern.This year's summit process is being held under the theme "navigating the future", with leaders expected to focus on strengthening cooperation and building resilience amid global uncertainties.Economic cooperation will also be an important part of India's engagement with Asean.Bilateral trade between India and the regional bloc stands at around $122 billion, making Asean one of India's major trading partners.India is also pushing for an early conclusion to the ongoing review of the India-Asean Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA), which New Delhi hopes will help address trade imbalances and improve market access.Tandon said discussions on the review were continuing, while acknowledging that negotiations involving multiple countries take time.Defence cooperation between India and Asean countries has also gained momentum in recent years.The Philippines became India's first foreign customer for the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile in 2022, signing a $375-million deal for three shore-based anti-ship missile batteries.Philippine defence secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr recently indicated that Manila was interested in acquiring additional systems and had submitted a wish list to India.On the South China Sea, India has maintained that any Asean-China Code of Conduct should be consistent with international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).The situation in Myanmar is another issue likely to feature in regional discussions. India has opposed diplomatic isolation of Myanmar, citing its geographical proximity, shared 1,643-km border and major connectivity projects, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project.Myanmar is expected to be represented in Manila by a foreign ministry official.The Manila visit has also drawn attention amid discussions around a possible Quad leaders' summit involving India, the US, Japan and Australia.US secretary of state Marco Rubio had indicated last month that the Quad summit was planned alongside the wider meetings in the Philippines. However, the MEA said it had no confirmed information on the meeting or a possible interaction between PM Modi and US President Donald Trump.A meeting between PM Modi and Trump, if scheduled, would come amid ongoing India-US trade negotiations and following recent setbacks for the Republican Party in the US midterm elections.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will travel to Manila on Monday for a two-day visit. He will attend the 23rd India-Asean Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit. Maritime security, regional stability and expanding trade ties are expected to be key focus areas at the meetings.

Article Title: Those using Form 6 to re-enroll won't be prosecuted: EC to SC

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has assured Supreme Court that all attempts will be made to include every eligible citizen in the electoral rolls and no prosecution would be launched against people whose names were deleted from the post-SIR draft electoral rolls, for using Form 6 for restoration of their names in the voters' lists.EC's stand, spelt out in an affidavit filed Saturday, is in sync with the Oct 26 assurance given by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana while hearing petitions relating to alleged large-scale deletion of voters in Maharashtra and Delhi. The CJI-led bench had said, "No one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voters' lists."Petitioners had highlighted voters' apprehension that they might be prosecuted for giving a false declaration in Form 6, which is used for enrolling new voters, that they had never been registered as voters before.EC said, "No prosecution will be launched against anyone for filing Form 6 merely on the ground that the applicant/elector was previously enrolled in the electoral roll(s) prior to the SIR and their names did not appear in the draft electoral rolls during the SIR."However, EC said those filling Form 6 to restore their names in the electoral rolls must ensure their names do not figure in the voters' lists in any other assembly or parliamentary constituency.Assuring the court that efforts have been intensified to register every eligible citizen as a voter, EC said, "A mechanism has also been directed to be put in place to ensure that no elector is deprived of the opportunity to get his/her name included in the final electoral roll, subject to fulfilment of the prescribed eligibility conditions, while taking due care to avoid duplication in enrolment."Accepting that there may have been errors in weeding out non-existent and dead voters from the electoral rolls through SIR, the commission said, "There are challenges on count of the large numbers involved, and also because the full data is being digitised. There have been and will be problems that arise from time to time and the commission remains alive to the need to ensure that all those who are eligible to vote find their name in the voters' lists but equally, to ensure that all inconsistencies in these lists are addressed. "On complaints about large-scale deletion of voters in Delhi through SIR in the ASDD (absent, shifted, duplicate and dead) category, EC said those left out of the draft electoral rolls could submit fresh enumeration forms to electoral registration officers or assistant EROs at their current residential place."Electors who have not shifted may submit the signed enumeration form with the statement giving the reason for the earlier non-submission of the enumeration form. They can submit it to the ERO/AERO/BLO in person or through family members. Online submission option with e-sign will be available on ECINET," it said.Those Delhi voters who have shifted residence from one constituency to another can submit fresh enumeration forms along with address proof to the ERO/AERO or avail the option of 'book a call with BLO', it said."Enumeration forms submitted by such electors shall be processed by EROs in accordance with Rule 21(1) of Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and the same EPIC number shall be re-assigned to them. An elector who has already submitted Form 6 during the SIR need not submit the enumeration form afresh," EC said.
Article Summary: EC's stand, spelt out in an affidavit filed Saturday, is in sync with the Oct 26 assurance given by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. The CJI-led bench had said, "No one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voters' lists"

NEW DELHI: Purity, hygiene and cleanliness are paramount for devotees during Chhath Puja . With God as their witness - quite literally in this case - devotees go to great lengths to observe strict hygiene while following elaborate rituals centred around the worship of the Sun deity over four days.In Delhi, devotees stepped into the sullied waters of the Yamuna, believing that their faith will protect them.The festival also provided a political stage, with Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta joining devotees at the Yamuna ghats and offering prayers to Chhathi Maiya. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, too, extended his wishes on the occasion of Sandhya Arghya.But as thousands gathered along the river's banks, the Yamuna underwent its annual public audit - with devotees standing waist-deep in its waters.Chhath Puja, rooted in devotion to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, is primarily observed by people from Bihar, eastern UP and Jharkhand.Observed over four days, the festival begins with Nahay-Khay, when devotees prepare simple, traditional food while observing strict personal hygiene and purity.This is followed by Kharna, when jaggery-based kheer and wheat rotis are prepared as prasad.After Kharna, devotees undertake a rigorous 36-hour nirjala fast, abstaining from both food and water.The rituals culminate in offerings of arghya to the setting Sun, followed by prayers to the rising Sun on the final day.Every year, as Chhath Puja approaches, the Yamuna becomes more than a river for Delhi.This year, BJP MP Manoj Tiwari took a dip in the Yamuna at Sonia Vihar, praising the cleanup under chief minister Rekha Gupta.“How can we not appreciate the work that has been done here?” he said. “There might be crocodiles in the water here, but crocodiles come in clean water.”AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar answered by floating an effigy of Tiwari at Kalindi Kunj and challenging him to bathe there, claiming that stretch was far more polluted.On Nahay Khay, the first day of the festival, a video purportedly showing dead fish near Sonia Vihar surfaced on social media.Delhi ministers accused AAP of staging it, alleging that party workers bought fish from the market and dumped them in the river.Delhi AAP chief Saurabh Bharadwaj denied this and demanded an inquiry on Friday, saying water samples had not yet been collected to establish the cause.The river has been a political flashpoint around Chhath before. Last year, AAP alleged that a temporary artificial pool at Vasudev Ghat was built to project a clean Yamuna ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s planned Chhath visit, which did not take place.Chhath's growing political importance has a lot to do with Delhi's changing demography. According to reports, continued migration from Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern UP has increased the share of the Purvanchali community to about 30 percent of Delhi's population.The festival offers political parties an opportunity to reach a sizeable constituency through a celebration deeply woven into its cultural identity.According to reports, the Delhi government is setting up 1,482 Chhath ghats across 996 locations. The growing prominence of a festival once largely observed within community networks reflects how it has become an important fixture on the capital's political calendar.The Yamuna's pollution becomes particularly visible around Chhath Puja, when devotees gather in large numbers along its banks to offer prayers.While talking to the Times of India, environmentalist Saumya Dutta said that the timing of Chhath coincides with a period when the river's flow has receded considerably after the monsoon, leaving less water to dilute the pollutants entering it.“During the days of Chhath Puja, tens of thousands of Delhi residents from Bihar and eastern UP, along with others, add huge amounts of pollutants, particularly detergents containing surfactants, which are common ingredients in soaps and detergents, as well as some industrial waste,” Dutta said.“Long after the peak monsoon flow, this is the period when the Yamuna's flow becomes very low. This low water flow, combined with high amounts of surfactants, causes large amounts of foam when the water is agitated. This becomes particularly visible during the huge influx of people and pollutants into this short 2% stretch of the Yamuna,” he said.According to Dutta, the 22-km stretch through the capital accounts for roughly 2% of the Yamuna's total length but contributes 70-80% of its overall pollution load.“Defaming agents and pre-Chhath cleaning do help for a very short period, but as the incoming pollution does not go down, this benefit is very short-term and vanishes quickly,” Dutta told TOI.“The major reason for the abject failure of Yamuna cleaning plans, as well as schemes like Namami Gange, is that the huge daily inflow of partially treated or even untreated sewage and industrial effluent into the river is not being tackled,” he added.In one of the most polluted major rivers of India, devotees will stand waist-deep, waiting for the Sun to set and rise the following day.But is it safe for a person to come in contact with such polluted river?According to Dr Srijan Garg immersion during Chhath can expose people to harmful bacteria, viruses and parasites through the skin, eyes, nose and ears, and sometimes through accidental ingestion."Devotees are exposed through the skin, eyes, nose, ear and sometimes by ingestion. However, the major exposure is through the skin and can cause various infections such as folliculitis, dermatitis, fungal infections," Dr. Garg told TOI.The water is full of untreated sewage water. so swallowing that water will affect the health of the individual. Some acute infections typhoid, hepatitis A or E, giardiasis, cholera. These usually present with diarrhoea, vomiting and pain abdomen," he added.Meanwhile, Dr. Ishan Singh said that people with cuts or open wounds are particularly vulnerable to infections."Industrial discharge may introduce heavy metals such as lead, mercury, arsenic and cadmium into river water. Depending on concentration and duration of exposure, these can affect the kidneys, liver and nervous system. Some chemicals may also irritate the skin and eyes," Dr. Singh told TOI."However, their actual presence and concentration at individual ghats must be confirmed through laboratory testing. A single brief exposure should not automatically be considered a cause of heavy-metal poisoning," he added.He also said that children, pregnant women, elderly people, diabetic patients and people with weakened immunity need particular attention.Dr. Singh also advised devotees to avoid swallowing river water, keep immersion time short and stay away from areas close to sewage discharge points. Those with open wounds should preferably avoid entering the water. After immersion, devotees should wash thoroughly with clean water and soap and change out of wet clothes.Chhath will end with prayers to the rising Sun, as devotees complete the four-day rituals with hopes and gratitude. However, the Yamuna's problems will remain long after the devotees leave the ghats.The wait for a cleaner river is likely to continue, with sewage and industrial waste flowing into it despite periodic cleaning drives and political promises.And when Chhath returns next year, the river will once again face its annual public audit, with the same questions over its cleanliness and safety likely to resurface.
Article Summary: Chhath Puja is rooted in devotion to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya. It is primarily observed by people from Bihar, eastern UP and Jharkhand. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta joined devotees at the Yamuna ghats.

SRINAGAR: Kashmiri movie veterans have shined a harsh light on Bollywood’s trite scripts confining J&K’s depiction to “scenic beauty, skullcaps that few in the Valley actually wear and AK-47s carried under pherans and long beards”, while calling for strengthening indigenous filmmaking.Speakers reeled off such gripes at a seminar organised in Srinagar on Saturday by Kashmir Music Club, run by popular singer Waheed Jeelani.“We have stronger stories here and there is a need to develop them,” actor Umar Imtiyaz said as he took potshots at Bollywood for dishing out its familiar fare of “skullcaps, long beards and AK-47s under pherans (long, loose-fitting garments worn by Kashmiris in winter)”. Imtiyaz argued that it was time to challenge such stereotypical representations.Echoing the sentiment, filmmaker Ayash Arif called for a focus on regional cinema that blends local concerns with a broader global outlook. He criticised J&K govt’s film policy, arguing it was more of a tourism blueprint aimed at encouraging filmmakers from elsewhere to shoot in the region due to its scenic beauty. What is needed, Arif said, is a roadmap aimed at promoting local productions.The 2022 policy offers several initiatives, including a single-window portal for shooting permissions and subsidies.It recalls the heady 1960s when blockbusters like Kashmir Ki Kali, Jab Jab Phool Khile, Himalay Ki God Mein and Janwar were shot in Srinagar and Gulmarg, followed by some international productions such as The Razor’s Edge in the 1980s.At the seminar, however, many felt the policy does not address requirements back home. “There is a lot for outside filmmakers in the policy but not much for local makers,” Arif said.Director Kapil Matoo, whose recent film Tasrufdar: Djinns of Kashmir won critical acclaim, urged local filmmakers to shed a sense of victimhood and recognise their own potential. “We must have our own industry here and start making films as we have stories of every shade,” Matoo said.Actor-director Mir Sarwar exhorted local artists not to depend on the limited opportunities offered by Doordarshan Srinagar and J&K Academy of Art. “We must help each other rather than wait for roles from filmmakers who come from outside,” Sarwar said. Cinematographer Shafqat Habib felt Kashmiri filmmakers must carve out a distinct identity.
Article Summary: Kashmiri movie veterans have shined a harsh light on Bollywood’s trite scripts. Speakers reeled off such gripes at a seminar organised in Srinagar on Saturday. “We have stronger stories here and there is a need to develop them,” actor Umar Imtiyaz said.

Article Title: '100% pure' or just marketing? What the law says about misleading food labels
Article Text:
Food labelling laws, consumer rights and regulatory mechanisms exist to tackle misleading claims and discrepancies in packaged food products

Raids alone cannot ensure food safety

What Indian law says about

misleading food labels

1. Ingredients must be declared in the correct order

2. When does a food product become misbranded?

Section 52 (misbranded food): Manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing or importing misbranded food for human consumption can attract a penalty of up to Rs 3 lakh.

Manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing or importing misbranded food for human consumption can attract a penalty of up to Rs 3 lakh. Section 53 (misleading advertisements): Publishing or participating in a misleading food advertisement can attract a penalty of up to Rs 10 lakh.

Publishing or participating in a misleading food advertisement can attract a penalty of up to Rs 10 lakh. Section 51 (sub-standard food): Food that fails prescribed compositional standards but is not necessarily unsafe can attract a penalty of up to Rs 5 lakh.

Can an online grocery platform be held responsible?

Product information must be displayed.

Misleading descriptions are prohibited.

Consumers have a statutory right to accurate information.

Fine print is not a shield

What should consumers do

Step 1: Keep the packaging and document the discrepancy

The wrapper, carton, bottle or jar. If still sealed, keep it unopened. Full-screen screenshots of the product title, ingredient claims, nutritional information and photographs shown in the app when the order was placed. The invoice and order details downloaded from the platform. Photographs of the batch or lot number, manufacturing date, expiry or Use By date, MRP and the 14-digit FSSAI licence number on the packet. Emails, in-app chats and other communications with the platform or manufacturer.

Step 2: Approach the platform's grievance officer

Step 3: Register a complaint with the National Consumer Helpline

Step 4: Report the violation directly to FSSAI

Step 5: Consider sending a legal notice

When to approach the Consumer Commission

What compensation and action can consumers seek

Why consumers still hesitate

The principal hurdles are procedural delays that sometimes take a toll on an average consumer. Anikita, senior associate, Chamber of Jain and Kumar

Food label more than a marketing claim

A food packet promises "100% pure" fruit juice, authentic honey or whole-grain biscuits, yet in India it has become a normal understanding that such claims are over the top.In a different scenario, the ingredients listed on an online grocery platform also differ from what arrives at the doorstep. With the online grocery shopping trend growing, these discrepancies are becoming a serious food safety and consumer protection concern.The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 , the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and the Legal Metrology Act, 2009, lay down obligations for manufacturers, sellers and e-commerce platforms.But it requires knowing what constitutes misleading labelling, understanding which authority to approach and preserving the right evidence.The latest FSSAI enforcement figures say that it suspended 1,133 licences, cancelled 52 and sealed 314 premises.Ashwin Bhadri, a national resource person for FSSAI says the real challenge begins after the inspection team leaves. Inspections and punitive action are necessary because they remind businesses that authorities are watching, but temporary fixes do not address the reasons behind repeated violations."A crackdown is an event. Food safety is a habit," Bhadri explains. "A suspension is a pause. What I wonder about is what changed inside the business during the pause. Was the pest-control contract fixed, or was the kitchen simply cleaned for the visit? Was the cause of the failure found, or only the symptom?"He says visible violations often point to deeper problems in raw material sourcing, supplier verification, cleaning practices and quality checks during manufacturing.Parliamentary figures for 2025-26 show the same gap."The wider numbers show where the challenge lies. The government told Parliament that of 2,23,808 food samples analysed in 2025-26, 40,023 were found non-conforming, close to one in five. The figures are provisional, and non-conforming covers a wide range, from misbranding to genuine adulteration. Convictions over the same period stood at 1,918. I would not read those two numbers as a ratio. But together they tell us something: the system is far better at finding problems than at seeing them through to a lasting fix," Bhadri observes.Three laws govern these responsibilities: the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and the Legal Metrology Act, 2009.The Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020, framed under Section 23 of the FSSAI Act, set the basic requirements for food labels.Ankita, senior associate, Chamber of Jain and Kumar, explains that ingredient disclosure remains a fundamental obligation:"In Under Regulation 5 of the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020, food manufacturers are required to declare ingredients on pre-packaged food products, generally in descending order of their composition by weight or volume. The law also mandates disclosures concerning allergens, nutritional information and food additives, wherever applicable. The 2026 amendments introduce additional labelling-related requirements, but do not remove the fundamental obligation to disclose ingredients," she says.Section 3(f) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, defines misbranded food, i.e., when a product is sold under a deceptive name, presented as a substitute for another food, or carries a statement, design or representation about its ingredients or composition that is false or misleading.For instance, a product marketed as "100% pure" that contains undeclared ingredients contradicting the claim could attract scrutiny under these provisions.Penalties depend on the violation:Under the licensing framework, including Regulation 2.1.8 of the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011, authorities can also suspend or cancel a food business licence for non-compliance.The manufacturer may argue the product was correctly labelled, while the platform may say the seller uploaded the description. But India's framework also covers online food businesses and e-commerce entities.The Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Amendment Regulations, 2018, which introduced provisions for e-commerce food business operators, require platforms to give consumers relevant product information before purchase.They also provide for a minimum remaining shelf life of 30% or 45 days before expiry, whichever applies, at the time of delivery.The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, place obligations on marketplaces and inventory-based platforms.Descriptions and advertisements must be consistent with the actual characteristics of the goods, which matters most when a listing claims "pure", "natural", "sugar-free" or "whole-grain".Section 2(9) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, recognises the right to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price of goods. Section 2(11) defines deficiency in service, and Section 2(47) deals with unfair trade practices.If the delivered product differs materially from the description at the time of purchase, the consumer may invoke these provisions, depending on the facts.The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) can investigate misleading advertisements and issue directions under Section 21.It can order their discontinuation or modification and impose penalties of up to Rs 10 lakh for a first contravention and up to Rs 50 lakh for subsequent ones.Regulation 4 of the 2020 Labelling and Display Regulations requires mandatory declarations to be clear, prominent, indelible and readily legible under normal conditions of purchase and use, and prescribes minimum font heights based on the area of the principal display panel.A manufacturer cannot rely on an inconspicuous disclaimer to avoid its labelling obligations."Fine print can sometimes be used to obscure material information and make important disclosures difficult for consumers to notice. However, statutory labelling requirements cannot be bypassed through disclaimers or inconspicuous disclosures,” says Ankita.“Mandatory declarations must comply with the prescribed requirements concerning visibility and legibility. Consumers can challenge misleading or inadequate disclosures before the relevant regulatory authorities and Consumer Commissions," Ankita adds.For a Rs 150 or Rs 600 grocery order, a regulator or consumer court can seem excessive.But consumers need not begin with litigation. India offers several administrative and pre-litigation routes.Do not throw away the packet or jar. Ankita says the packaging, invoice, batch details and photographs can become key evidence:"A consumer can report the violation to FSSAI or the concerned State Food Safety Department. They can also approach the National Consumer Helpline (1915) or file a complaint before the appropriate Consumer Commission. It is important to preserve the product packaging, purchase invoice, batch number and photographs of the label as evidence," she advises.Preserve five categories of evidence:Under Rule 4(4) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, every e-commerce entity must prominently display the name and contact details of its Grievance Officer. The officer must acknowledge a complaint within 48 hours and redress it within one month.If the platform does not resolve the issue, approach the National Consumer Helpline (NCH), run by the Department of Consumer Affairs. Call 1915, use the NCH mobile app, or visit consumerhelpline.gov.in For issues of ingredients, food safety, misbranding or misleading food claims, complaints can go through the Food Safety Connect mobile app or the Food Safety Compliance System portal at foscos.fssai.gov.in Provide the product's 14-digit FSSAI licence number and upload photographs of the alleged violation. Unlike a routine refund request, a regulatory complaint can lead to scrutiny by the jurisdictional Designated Officer or Food Safety Officer, who may inspect the manufacturing facility, warehouse or dark store and initiate proceedings under the Act.A written legal notice to the manufacturer and the platform can identify the discrepancy and cite provisions such as Regulation 5 of the 2020 Labelling and Display Regulations and Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.It puts the parties on formal notice of the allegations and potential consequences. Ankita says litigation need not come first:If the manufacturer or platform refuses to act, consumers can go to the appropriate Consumer Commission. Under Section 34 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has pecuniary jurisdiction where the consideration paid does not exceed Rs 50 lakh.Complaints can be filed on the e-Daakhil portal at edaakhil.nic.in, which allows submission of documents from home and virtual proceedings where permitted, without necessarily engaging a lawyer.Under Section 38(2)(c) of the Act, a Commission can direct that a sample be sent to an appropriate laboratory. Consumers can also submit an independent test report from an NABL-accredited laboratory.Under Section 39(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Commissions can direct refunds, replacement of goods and compensation for loss or injury, including mental agony, plus litigation costs.They can also order a business to discontinue an unfair trade practice, withdraw hazardous or misdescribed goods, and pay punitive damages into the Consumer Welfare Fund. A complaint about one purchase can therefore have wider implications if the same practice affects other consumers.Pursuing a complaint is not always straightforward. Proceedings take time, and it can be hard to establish exactly how a product's composition differs from its declared ingredients.Manufacturers may call the discrepancy a technical or inadvertent labelling error, and actual composition disputes may need independent testing. The low cost of a single grocery purchase can also discourage complaints."The principal hurdles are procedural delays that sometimes take a toll on an average consumer. Sometimes, establishing the violation, proving the loss or injury suffered are some other common hurdles. Companies may sometimes argue that a discrepancy is merely a technical or inadvertent labelling error. Therefore, proper documentation and demonstrating how the violation affects consumer rights become particularly important," notes Ankita.She further adds, "I strongly encourage consumers to call out companies engaging in misleading practices, provided their allegations are supported by facts and evidence. Public accountability creates pressure on companies to follow statutory requirements. Consumer awareness is one of the strongest deterrents against unfair trade practices, and companies must understand that regulatory compliance is not optional.You might have also seen a surge of such cases in present times where FSSAI has suo moto taken actions against companies who are violating the norms.”For food businesses, compliance cannot stop at correcting labels after an inspection or controversy.For consumers, the key safeguard is to look beyond the claims shown prominently on a packet or app. Ankita says transparency is a legal obligation, not a voluntary promise:"I would emphasise that consumers have a fundamental right to know what they are purchasing and consuming. Transparency in labelling is not a privilege offered by companies; it is a statutory obligation. With evolving FSSAI regulations and increasing consumer awareness, companies must prioritise transparency and compliance over marketing strategies. Ultimately, an informed consumer is the strongest safeguard against unfair trade practices," she concludes.The next time a grocery order arrives, checking the back of the packet may be just as important as checking the price on the screen.
Article Summary: Food labelling laws, consumer rights and regulatory mechanisms exist to tackle misleading claims and discrepancies in packaged food products. With the online grocery shopping trend growing, these discrepancies are becoming a serious food safety and consumer protection concern. The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and the Legal Metrology Act, 2009, lay down obligations for manufacturers, sellers and e-commerce platforms.

Article Title: Air India Delhi-SFO was 2.5 hours away from destination when US ATC failed; all 5 AI flights landed on time
Article Text:
All 5 AI flights landed safely at their destinations and on time

Poll Vote & Share your view How concerned are you about air travel disruptions due to ground stops? Very concerned Somewhat concerned Not very concerned Not concerned at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Air India ’s Delhi-San Francisco (SFO) nonstop was over the Pacific and just about two hours away from its destination, when the US ordered a ground stop on Friday the 13th when Uncle Sam’s outdated air traffic control (ATC) systems began to fail. There were four other AI nonstops, all to New York via the Atlantic route, but they were further away from their destinations. Luckily, the US Air Traffic Control System Command Centre (ATCSCC) advisory issued at 2.24 am (IST of Nov 14) to announce the ground stop said “inbound international flights will be managed on a case by case basis” while asking all departing flights to remain on ground. The Boeing 777 (VT-ALS) landed in SFO at 5 am.“As soon as the ATCSCC advisory was issued at 2.24 am, AI flight operations buzzed the leadership team and they went into a huddle. SFO flight was the closest to its destination and proceeded since the pilots, who were in touch with Oakland control at that time, were not told to divert as per the advisory which meant the B777 will be allowed to land,” said people in the know.AI kept a close eye on the developing situation and the four other flights — one each from Delhi and Mumbai to Newark (EWR) and JFK — kept proceeding to their destinations.The outage lasted about five hours and these all landed as per schedule.Of the five return flights these aircraft were to operate back home, only SFO-Delhi (via Kolkata) was delayed by about 2 hours and 40 minutes due to congestion at SFO. “All the other flights, two each out of EWR and JFK, operated on time,” said an official, adding Saturday-Sunday night departures were also on time except for the delayed arrival from SFO.AI senior pilots said this is the second time in less than four years that US faced an air traffic communication issue, although Friday the 13th was by far the most serious one. On Jan 10, 2023, the US Federal Aviation Administration was unable to issue notice to airmen (NOTAM) for some hours and it had to activate a hotline to manage the situation then. The FAA subsequently traced the problem to files unintentionally deleted by contract personnel while correcting synchronisation between the primary and backup databases.Following Friday’s failure, the US is prioritising international flights over domestic ones and the situation will take some days to recover as there will be a serious ripple effect. While Air India is the only Indian operator that flies to the US, two US carriers — United and American — have a daily each between Delhi and New York. Rest of the connectivity is provided by onestops of Gulf, European and southeast Asian carriers.Other airlines’ flights were also impacted.“Given the scale of the failure, the impact was massive. I was listening to ground control at JFK when the issue happened just before 4 pm EST (New York time) Friday. There were a lot of frustrated pilots and controllers. Hundreds of pilots were asking, ‘what’s the delay reason,’. Initially controller couldn’t give a reason and just said, ‘nationwide stop.’ Later it was determined a communication problem,” said a pilot who was in New York at that time.“Due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety, attention all aircraft operators: By order of the Federal Aviation Command Centre, all airports are ground stopped,” the ATCSCC advisory announcing the failure had said.
Article Summary: Air India’s Delhi-San Francisco (SFO) nonstop was over the Pacific and just about two hours away from its destination when the US ordered a ground stop on Friday the 13th. There were four other AI nonstops, all to New York via the Atlantic route, but they were further away from their destinations. All 5 AI flights landed safely at their destinations and on time.

Article Title: 'No place for goons': CM Adhikari's warning to criminals after encounter of Shantiniketan accused
Article Text:
CM Suvendu Adhikari defends Ratan Sheikh encounter

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday warned criminals and people possessing illegal firearms to leave the state. His warning came after Ratan Sheikh, the prime accused in the Santiniketan shooting case, was killed in a police encounter in Birbhum's Nanoor.Speaking to news agency ANI, Adhikari said Sheikh had opened fire at police personnel when they attempted to arrest him. He said the police took necessary action in response."He shot at the police, and the police did what needed to be done on the spot. It would not be appropriate for me to comment on this. There is no place for goons and rapists in West Bengal," Adhikari said.Issuing a warning to criminals and those possessing illegal firearms, he added, "Even now, whatever remaining goons and those with illegal arms are left, flee from here; leave immediately. There is no place for them here."Sheikh was accused of opening fire at a police team that went to arrest him in connection with the Santiniketan shooting incident. The firing took place on Friday evening in the Layek Bazar area of Bolpur.Three police personnel had reached the area to apprehend Sheikh. However, he allegedly opened fire after spotting them, injuring constable Biswajit Das in his left leg. Sheikh fled the spot and had been absconding since the incident.Sheikh was killed in a police encounter in Nanoor on Sunday. Adhikari described him as a dreaded criminal and said 36 cases had been registered against him. Sheikh had been granted bail in a robbery case and returned to the area last Friday.Following the shooting, Adhikari visited injured constable Biswajit Das at Bardhaman Medical College and Hospital. Doctors said his condition was stable.
Article Summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari warned criminals and people possessing illegal firearms to leave the state. His warning came after Ratan Sheikh, the prime accused in the Santiniketan shooting case, was killed in a police encounter in Birbhum's Nanoor.

Article Title: 'Well-planned conspiracy': BJP refutes reports of 209-candidate list for upcoming UP elections
Article Text:
The BJP said its candidate selection process for the 2027 UP polls has not yet begun and dismissed the reports as fabricated

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Uttar Pradesh unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Sunday rejected reports claiming that a list of 209 candidates for the 2027 assembly elections had been prepared and sent to the party's central leadership, calling them fabricated and part of a "well-planned conspiracy"."For the past few days, certain media outlets, individuals, and institutions have been continuously circulating news regarding an alleged list of 209 candidates of the Bharatiya Janata Party, Uttar Pradesh, being prepared and sent to the central leadership in the context of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. This is completely untrue, baseless, imaginary, and fabricated. The BJP outrightly refutes this fake and false news," news agency ANI quoted the statement as saying.Describing the reports as a "well-planned conspiracy", the statement alleged that some people were spreading rumours to create confusion, uncertainty and fear among party workers. It urged office-bearers, workers and the public not to rely on unverified reports and to follow information shared through authorised party platforms.The party said its candidate selection process had not yet begun. It added that the BJP follows a structured organisational process for choosing candidates for assembly and other elections.The joint statement was signed by chief minister Yogi Adityanath and state BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary.Earlier on Sunday, Chaudhary had also denied that the BJP had finalised names for 209 constituencies. Speaking to reporters, he said he had not held any meetings to prepare such a list.“I do not know the source of this news... As the State President of the Bharatiya Janata Party, I have not held any such meetings with anyone,” Chaudhary said.He outlined the party's candidate selection procedure, saying inputs are first collected at the district and regional levels before being discussed by the state core committee and election committee. The recommendations are then sent to Delhi, where the Parliamentary Board takes the final call.“The BJP is not a family-run party where a single individual can make such decisions; rather, the process is entirely collective,” he said.Chaudhary added that the party had followed the same organisational approach for the past 50 years, with decisions taken through consultation and consensus.
Article Summary: The Uttar Pradesh unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Sunday rejected reports claiming that a list of 209 candidates for the 2027 assembly elections had been prepared and sent to the party's central leadership. The party said its candidate selection process had not yet begun.

Article Title: 'You brought them in dumper truck': J&K BJP MLA's emotional outburst over handling of slain SPOs' bodies
Article Text:
'If an officer allows our mortal remains to be treated with indignity, what do you think the terrorists will do to them?' she asked

NEW DELHI: Kishtwar BJP MLA Shagun Parihar criticised J&K authorities over the handling of the mortal remains of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) killed in Kishtwar district. She alleged that their bodies were brought to the area in a dumper truck and handled with indignity."You brought the bodies of our people here in a dumper truck... Is this the value of our jawans?" Parihar said while interacting with police personnel over the recovery and transportation of the bodies. She also questioned why senior officials had not responded sooner to the families' concerns."It has been three days... If an officer allows our mortal remains to be treated with indignity, what do you think the terrorists will do to them?" she said, expressing anguish over the treatment of the deceased personnel.The BJP MLA also spoke about the family members of the slain SPOs, saying that a daughter who had been waiting for her father's body. "I keep thinking of that daughter who has been weeping for the last three days... A daughter who lost her father—she came here today, three days later, and only after the LG himself asked her," she said."You didn’t even show up here until we approached the Lieutenant Governor—until we knocked on the doors of the authorities in Delhi," Parihar alleged, adding, "with a heavy heart i must say our officers our officers were disrespected".Speaking later, Parihar also demanded an inquiry into the transportation of the bodies in a dumper truck, saying that anyone who sacrificed their life for the country deserved respect and a dignified farewell. "There should be an inquiry and investigation into the officers and everyone involved, so that such incidents are not repeated," she said.The bodies of Rashpal Kumar, 45, and Bobby Chand, 57, were recovered from the remote forests of Kishtwar on Thursday. Both were residents of Kiyar Dachhan and were posted with the Special Operations Group (SOG) in the Kiyar sector.The two SPOs had gone missing on November 10 while travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah for rotation duty. A search operation was launched after they failed to reach their destination. Their bodies were found with bullet injuries, while their service rifles were missing.

NEW DELHI: Govt spending on healthcare has more than tripled from Rs 1.3 lakh crore in 2013-14 to Rs 4.1 lakh crore in 2023-24, while the share of medical expenses borne directly by households has fallen from 64.2% to 42.7% of total health expenditure over the decade. Despite the decline, families continue to shoulder a substantial burden, paying Rs 4 lakh crore out of their own pockets in 2023-24, according to the latest National Health Accounts (NHA) estimates.The share of govt health expenditure (GHE) in total health expenditure increased from 28.6% to 43.5% during the same period. Per capita govt health spending also rose more than two-and-a-half times, from Rs 1,042 to Rs 2,959, according to NHA 2023-24, which is the eleventh round of health expenditure estimates.The report, which tracks financial flows across the country's healthcare system, estimates India's total health expenditure at Rs 9.52 lakh crore in 2023-24, equivalent to 3.29% of GDP, or Rs 6,801 per person. Of this, current health expenditure accounted for Rs 8.37 lakh crore (87.9%), while capital expenditure stood at Rs 1.15 lakh crore (12.1%).State govts continued to be the largest contributors to public health spending, accounting for nearly 68% of total govt health expenditure, compared with around 32% contributed by Centre.GHE amounted to 1.43% of GDP during 2023-24, said the report prepared by NHA Technical Secretariat under National Health Systems Resource Centre (NHSRC).The estimates also show an increase in social security expenditure on health, which includes govt-funded health insurance schemes, medical reimbursements for govt employees and social health insurance programmes. Its share in total health expenditure rose from 6% in 2013-14 to 11% in 2023-24.Private health insurance expenditure stood at Rs 97,167 crore, accounting for 10.2% of total health expenditure. Expenditure under all govt-financed health insurance schemes combined was Rs 33,385 crore.An analysis of where healthcare money is spent shows that private hospitals accounted for 31.91% of current health expenditure, against 16.77% for govt hospitals. Pharmacies accounted for another 20.6%, with expenditure amounting to Rs 1.72 lakh crore.Pharmaceutical expenditure, including prescribed and over-the-counter medicines and drugs supplied during inpatient and outpatient treatment, accounted for 30.2% of current health expenditure.Primary care accounted for around 46% of current health expenditure, followed by secondary care at around 35% and tertiary care at 14%.
Article Summary: Spending on healthcare has more than tripled from Rs 1.3 lakh crore in 2013-14. Share of medical expenses borne directly by households has fallen from 64.2% to 42.7%. Families continue to shoulder a substantial burden, paying Rs 4 lakh crore out of their own pockets.

Article Title: From Sonia-Natwar row to Advani's Jinnah remarks: 5 political memoirs that stirred storm
Article Text:
Political memoirs often bring long-held views, personal accounts and contested versions of history back into the spotlight

Natwar Singh's One Life Is Not Enough

Natwar Singh on Rahul Gandhi’s role in Sonia’s decision not to become PM

LK Advani's My Country, My Life

Pranab Mukherjee's The Presidential Years

Pranab Mukherjee on the decline of charismatic leadership in Indian politics
